ordinary_frame.basis: This source orders the Mandatum antiphons and prayer after the Gospel and before the Offertory, then appoints the hymn for the Translation after the Postcommunion. The generic Ordinary frame cannot represent that middle rite and concluding procession. A specialized frame has not yet been modeled, so the generic frame is withheld and all source rows remain in their printed order.

propers.name: Mandatum Antiphon 8
propers.text:
Ubi caritas et amor, Deus ibi est. V. Congregavit nos in unum Christi amor.
V. Exsultemus et in ipso jucundemur. V. Timeamus et amemus Deum vivum. V. Et
ex corde diligamus nos sincero. Et repetitur antiphona: Ubi caritas et amor,
Deus ibi est. V. Simul ergo cum in unum congregamur: V. Ne nos mente
dividamur, caveamus. V. Cessent jurgia maligna, cessent lites. V. Et in
medio nostri sit Christus Deus. Et repetitur antiphona: Ubi caritas et amor,
Deus ibi est. V. Simul quoque cum beatis videamus V. Glorianter vultum tuum,
Christe Deus: V. Gaudium, quod est immensum atque probum, V. Saecula per
infinita saeculorum. Amen.

provenance.locator: editorial-projection artifact physical lines 17-22; antecedent printed p. 164 (Feria V. in Coena Domini, after the Mandatum versicles); text-layer lines 31892-31907
provenance.provenance_authority: Triptych editorial projection verified by page-image collation against the 1962 target edition
provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after `Domine` and none after `et` (`et quia tu`); 1962 sets both; 1862 sets a comma after `hic nobis`; 1962 does not; CONCLUSION LENGTH: 1862 `qui vivis et regnas Deus, per omnia saecula saeculorum`; 1962 `qui vivis et regnas in saecula saeculorum`. The 1862's is the longer form here -- the usual direction is reversed.; 1862 layer damage: `aespi-cias` for `despicias` (line 31897) and `interioria` for `interiora` (line 31903); letterforms inferred, not read. Corroboration: 1604 at line 26802 prints `...irum interiora lauentur peccata. Quod ipse praestare digneri[s]...` (long s as f/i throughout, u for v), which supplies `interiora laventur peccata` at the same place and disposes of the 1862 layer's `interioria`. Recorded limitation: Confidence is medium only because two words (`despicias`, `interiora`) were inferred from damaged letterforms rather than read; the 1604 supplies the second at the same point in the same prayer. The conclusion difference is a length difference in one rubrical formula (`qui vivis et regnas ...`), not a different formula, so it stays inside the pilot's settled tolerance. The 1862 prints this prayer after the Mandatum performed AFTER Mass and after the stripping of the altars; the 1955 rite moves the Mandatum inside Mass after the homily. Placement moved; the words did not.

propers.name: Prayer of the Mandatum
propers.text:
Adesto, Domine, quaesumus, officio servitutis nostrae: et, quia tu
discipulis tuis pedes lavare dignatus es, ne despicias opera manuum tuarum,
quae nobis retinenda mandasti: ut, sicut hic nobis et a nobis exteriora
abluuntur inquinamenta; sic a te omnium nostrum interiora laventur peccata.
Quod ipse praestare digneris, qui vivis et regnas in saecula saeculorum. R.
Amen.
